Today: 2026-05-25
ADR-0042: Region and residency model for the Kelp robot-telemetry pipeline. Project: Kelp (Ardent Robotics fleet telemetry). This record concerns Kelp alone; decisions by other Ardent teams are noted for context. Status: proposed - decision pending. Date: 22 May 2026. Author: Sanna Virtanen. Reviewers: Marco Bellini, Joy Nakamura.

Context
Kelp collects telemetry from autonomous floor-cleaning robots operating in customer sites - airports, hospitals and shopping centres - and powers the fleet-health dashboard, predictive maintenance alerts and monthly usage reports. The pipeline, storage layout and dashboards are built and run in our development account with synthetic robot data. Launch to customers was planned for the end of June, when the first hospital contract (with the Rheinland Kliniken group) starts.

The open question is where telemetry is stored and processed. Some robots carry cameras for obstacle detection. We do not store images, but obstacle events include coarse position data inside hospital wards, and Rheinland's data-protection officer considers that it may count as health-adjacent personal data.

Options
1. Single EU region (Frankfurt) for all customers.
2. Per-customer residency: each customer's data stays in a region it chooses, with separate storage accounts.
3. Process at the edge: robots aggregate events locally and send only counts, no positions.

Analysis
Option 1 is cheapest and simplest to operate. Option 2 satisfies any residency demand but roughly doubles infrastructure cost for small customers. Option 3 removes the personal-data question entirely but kills the heat-map feature that operations managers ranked as the most valuable in research.

Current position
We cannot choose between these options on our own. Rheinland's contract makes the residency model subject to approval by its data-protection officer, and our legal team has advised that we must not provision production storage or ingest any customer telemetry until that approval is in writing. We sent the DPO our data-flow description and a draft data-processing agreement for all three options on April 30. On May 18 her office replied that the review has been added to its queue, without giving a date. Until we have her answer, Kelp cannot provision the production accounts, connect a single customer robot or run the acceptance test with Rheinland, because every one of those steps depends on which option is chosen. Marco checked whether we could launch with another customer first, but the three other signed customers have all asked for the same model as Rheinland, so there is no customer we can safely onboard ahead of the decision.

Decisions by other Ardent teams (context only)
- The navigation team cancelled its plan to stream lidar point clouds to the cloud, so Kelp will not receive them.
- The charging-dock firmware release is two weeks late; it only affects how often robots report battery data.
- The customer-portal team finished single sign-on for enterprise customers in May.

What we are doing meanwhile
Sanna keeps the synthetic environment running so the dashboards can be demonstrated. Joy is preparing infrastructure templates for all three options so that, once there is an answer, the chosen one can be deployed. No further Kelp features are being started.

Review
Reviewers will reconvene within two days of receiving the DPO's response. Comments to #kelp-arch.

PRD - Pinecrest patient portal: online appointment self-scheduling. Milestone review, 2 September 2026. This PRD covers the self-scheduling project for the Pinecrest Health portal; other portal workstreams appear in the dependencies section.

Problem
About 62 percent of calls to Pinecrest's central booking line are routine appointment requests that could be handled online. Average wait on the line was 11 minutes in July. Patients can already see their upcoming appointments in the portal but cannot book, move or cancel them without phoning.

Goals
- Patients can book follow-up and routine visits with their own care team in primary care, dermatology and physiotherapy.
- Patients can reschedule or cancel up to 24 hours before a visit.
- Reduce booking-line call volume by 25 percent within six months.

Contract and deadline
Pinecrest's agreement with the regional health authority funds the project on condition that self-scheduling is live for all primary-care clinics by September 30, 2026.

Design
The booking flow was usability-tested with 20 patients, including six over 70 and three screen-reader users. Median time to book was 2 minutes 10 seconds. The main change after testing was to show the clinician's photo next to each slot, which older patients said reassured them.

Integration with the EHR
Self-scheduling reads open slots and writes bookings through the EHR vendor's scheduling API version 3, which adds the visit-type rules our clinics rely on. The vendor committed to delivering v3 to Pinecrest's test environment on August 3. The vendor delivered v3 on August 31, four weeks after its commitment; integration testing started on September 1 and is progressing, and the end-to-end test with three pilot clinics is now scheduled for late September. Primary-care go-live for all clinics is re-planned for October 27, almost four weeks after the funding deadline, and dermatology and physiotherapy move to December. Lucia has notified the health authority and asked how the funding condition will be applied.

Milestones
M1 Design complete - June 30 (done).
M2 Portal front end complete - July 31 (done).
M3 EHR integration and pilot clinics - August 31.
M4 All primary-care clinics - by September 30.
M5 Dermatology and physiotherapy - October.

Today: 2026-03-02
PRD: Orchard - bank-account aggregation for the Pennywise budgeting app. Revision 6, 2 March 2026. This document is about Orchard only; adjacent Pennywise initiatives are mentioned in section 7.

1. Summary
Pennywise users currently type in their transactions or import CSV files. Orchard lets them connect their UK bank accounts through open banking so transactions flow in automatically and categories update without effort. Orchard was planned to launch to all UK users in April 2026.

2. Users and problems
In the January survey, 58 percent of churned users said manual entry was the reason they stopped using the app. Users who import CSVs at least weekly retain at twice the rate of those who do not, which suggests automatic import could have a large effect.

3. Requirements
- Connect current accounts and credit cards from the nine largest UK banks at launch.
- Refresh transactions at least four times a day.
- Re-consent flow every 90 days, as the regulations require.
- Users can disconnect a bank at any time and choose to delete imported transactions.
- Merchant names are cleaned and categorised with the existing rules engine.

4. Design
The connect flow was tested with 14 users in February. All but one completed it without help; the person who struggled was confused by the bank's own login screen, which we cannot change. Visual design is final.

5. Engineering status
The aggregation partner's sandbox is integrated: test accounts connect, transactions import and are categorised, and re-consent reminders are scheduled correctly. The merchant-name cleaner was retrained on sandbox data and reaches 91 percent accuracy on the review set.

6. Regulatory dependency and current position
To receive bank data for our own users, Pennywise must be registered as an account information service provider with the Financial Conduct Authority. We submitted the application in November. In February the FCA asked a further set of questions about our safeguarding of customer data and our complaints procedure; we answered on February 20, and the FCA has not yet replied or indicated when it will decide. The aggregation partner will not issue production credentials to an unregistered firm, and we may not connect a single real customer account until registration is granted. Every remaining milestone - the friends-and-family test with real accounts, the security penetration test against production credentials, and the public launch - depends on those credentials, and there is no interim route that the partner or our compliance advisers consider acceptable. The engineering team has finished everything it can do in the sandbox and has been lent to the iOS widgets work while we wait.

7. Adjacent initiatives
- Pennywise Premium pricing change: delayed to May while the finance team reruns the price-elasticity test.
- Shared household budgets: cancelled in January after the prototype test showed low interest; it would have used Orchard data but Orchard never depended on it.
- iOS home-screen widgets: in progress, expected in March.
- Android accessibility fixes: completed February 26.

8. Metrics after launch
Primary: 30-day retention of users who connect at least one account. Secondary: share of active users with a connected account, number of manual transactions per user, support tickets about missing transactions.

9. Risks
Some banks' interfaces return pending transactions inconsistently; the partner normalises most cases. Users may distrust sharing bank data with a small app; the connect flow explains the read-only access clearly.

10. Sign-off
Product: Harriet Cole. Engineering: Vikram Sethi. Compliance: Mariana Duarte. Design: Ollie Brandt.

text:
Today: 2026-09-14
PRD: Marlin click-and-collect lockers - milestone update, 14 September 2026. The Marlin locker programme is the subject of this PRD; other Hartwell Stores initiatives appear only where they touch it.

Summary of intent
Marlin was approved in February to place temperature-controlled pickup lockers in 40 Hartwell supermarkets so online grocery customers can collect orders at any hour. The planned deliverables were: locker hardware in all 40 stores, a pickup flow in the Hartwell app, and staff tooling to load lockers from the back of the store. Original rollout: pilot in 5 stores in October, remaining 35 by end of January 2027.

Customer research
Survey of 3,100 online-grocery customers in April: 41 percent said they would use a locker at least once a month; the most cited reason was collecting after work when stores are busy. Willingness to pay a collection fee was low (under 15 percent), so the business case assumed free collection funded by reduced delivery volume.

Milestones so far
- Hardware vendor selected (Fridgelock), contract signed in May.
- App pickup flow designed and usability-tested in June; build 60 percent complete.
- Staff loading tool prototype tested in two stores in August.
- Site surveys done for 32 of 40 stores.

Programme decision, 8 September
At the quarterly investment review, the Chief Operating Officer presented updated delivery economics: the third-party delivery partner cut its per-order price by 35 percent in August, which removes most of the saving the lockers were meant to produce. The COO terminated the Marlin programme. No lockers will be installed, the pilot in October will not take place, and the app pickup flow will not be released. Fridgelock has been notified under the contract's termination-for-convenience clause, and the two prototype units will be returned by the end of the month.

What we are keeping
The store-level stock-reservation API built for Marlin also helps the rapid-delivery team, so it stays in production. The usability findings from the June tests are being handed to the app team for the curbside-pickup screens.

Other initiatives referenced in earlier versions
- Curbside pickup (owned by the app team) is two weeks late because of a parking-bay sensor issue; it continues independently of Marlin.
- The in-store returns kiosk initiative was cancelled in July and is listed here only because it shared a hardware buyer with Marlin.
- The Hartwell rapid-delivery service is waiting on a licence from one city council before it can launch there.

Financials
Spend to date: 1.9 million of the 6.4 million budget. The termination fee owed to Fridgelock is 180,000, already accrued. Unspent budget returns to the capital pool for the Q4 allocation round.

People
Product manager Isabel Moreau moves to the curbside-pickup team. The two app engineers on the pickup flow join the loyalty squad on October 1. Hardware lead Dmitri Volkov stays until the prototype units are collected.

Document history
v1 Feb 12 (approval), v2 May 20 (vendor), v3 Aug 15 (site surveys), v4 Sep 14 (this edition). Questions to Isabel Moreau.
